transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Sarah Liu (Willowgate), Trevor Malik (Willowgate CISO), Aisha Khan (Platform Eng), Evan Price (Procurement), Noah Reed (Legal)

Summary: High-level discovery focused on data residency and compliance guardrails. Willowgate is evaluating tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments for an internal risk‑scoring LLM. Primary concerns: region-locking, key management, audit/evidence trails, log redaction and retention, and segmentation across regulated funds. Customer asked for architecture diagrams, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and a KMS deep dive; Redwood agreed to run a short benchmark and share docs.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. Quick intros, then we'll jump into specifics around residency and the controls you need.
[00:12] Sarah (Willowgate): Hi all, Sarah here. We're trying to map options for serving our risk scoring model — low latency is important but regulators want strict residency and audit trails, so tradeoffs.
[00:24] Miguel (Redwood SE): Great — can you give a bit more color on the workload? Batch scoring? Real-time scoring behind an API? Sequence lengths? PII in prompts?
[00:37] Aisha (Platform): Mostly real-time, sub-250ms tail is a nice-to-have for some flows but 500–700ms is acceptable for scoring. Prompts will contain account IDs, masked SSNs occasionally, and transaction snippets — so we treat them as regulated.
[00:55] Trevor (CISO): And from legal/reg, some jurisdictions require keys and logs to remain in-EC2-region X; we cannot ship raw prompts cross-border. Also retention windows: audit logs need to be kept for seven years for a subset of activity.
[01:13] Lena: Understood. I'm going to lay out how Redwood approaches Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and then Miguel can dig into key management and logging.
[01:25] Lena: Hosted gives fastest time to value but has multi-tenant control plane — we offer options for regional pinning and strict egress rules, but for the strictest requirements Private is usually the fit.
[01:39] Evan (Procurement): By Private you mean customer-managed VPC plus on-prem options? What's the level of separation?
[01:46] Miguel: Yes. Private offers a customer-dedicated control plane in your VPC; compute can run on dedicated GPU pools in your account or in Redwood-hosted appliances that are network-isolated. There's also an on-prem bundle for air-gapped scenarios.
[02:02] Noah (Legal): Important for us — if we run Private, can Redwood still access logs for support? We need to control who can see PII.
[02:11] Priya (Redwood SE): You can configure role-based access controls. For Private deployments the control plane is customer-owned, and Redwood's support access is gated via just-in-time access, audited, and can be restricted to metadata-only if you prefer. Support relationships are contractually scoped.
[02:29] Trevor: Okay. On KMS — we have an HSM with key residency requirements. Can we bring our own keys and ensure they never leave region?
[02:38] Miguel: Customers can BYOK (bring your own key) via our KMS integrations — you can point to an AWS KMS key with regional scope or a customer-managed HSM. For complete assurance there are two patterns: keep keys in your cloud account and use remote encryption APIs, or use a Redwood-managed key for certain non‑sensitive artifacts while storing critical keys in your HSM.
[02:58] Sarah: So in the first pattern the tokenization or encryption happens in our account before anything ever goes to Redwood?
[03:05] Miguel: Correct — we support client-side encryption workflows and prefixes are stripped before they reach model-servers. There is some engineering overhead, but it ensures raw PII never transits Redwood systems.
[03:18] [noise, crosstalk]
[03:22] Aisha: On logs — we need per-tenant logging streams, with the ability to redact sensitive fields automatically. How do you do redaction? Is it regex-based or model-assisted?
[03:32] Priya: We support configurable redaction pipelines. Default is configurable scrubbing rules (regex, tokenization) and you can plug in model-assisted classifiers for higher fidelity. For Private, you can run the pipeline inside your VPC so raw logs never leave region.
[03:47] Trevor: Retention controls? We need different retention windows per dataset: example, PII should be purged after 30 days, while metadata/audit trails kept for 7 years. Can Redwood support per-stream retention?
[03:58] Miguel: Yes — retention is per-log-stream. You can configure retention policies and also set automatic tiering/archival. For hosted customers there's a managed SLA; for dedicated/private you control the retention and archival location.
[04:12] Lena: To be clear on tradeoffs: Hosted is easiest but has constraints around in-region guarantees and vendor-managed keys. Dedicated gives isolation at compute layer and predictable throughput; Private gives you full network and key control but costs and ops overhead are higher.
[04:27] Sarah: We also have legal holds and e-discovery needs. If regulator wants raw artifacts for a specific incident, what's the path?
[04:36] Priya: For Private, you control the evidence. For dedicated/hosted, we maintain audit logs and can provide exports but raw PII export is governed by contract and usually requires a secure transfer process. We recommend a pre-agreed runbook for legal holds.
[04:52] Trevor: Does Redwood provide tamper-evident audit logs (append-only) or do we need to wire in our own WORM storage?
[04:59] Miguel: We have append-only audit logs backed by cloud storage with integrity checks and signed audit entries; customers can also configure direct streaming to their WORM/S3 bucket to meet internal evidence requirements.
[05:13] [00:05:13] Sarah: Can we discuss network egress and region-locking? We need to ensure requests physically terminate in our EU region for EU customers.
[05:22] Lena: Yes. Hosted supports region routing but for guarantees around physical residency and operator access, Private in-region deployment is the recommended path. Dedicated can be pinned to a region as well, but operator access will be through Redwood-staffed paths unless you elect Private control plane.
[05:38] Aisha: What about fallback and graceful degradation? If a regional cluster is down do requests fall back to other regions? That would violate residency.
[05:46] Miguel: Good catch. Fallback is policy-driven — we can disable cross-region fallback for sensitive routes. If you disable fallback, you'd prefer to fail closed rather than risk cross-border processing.
[05:58] Evan: How does pricing change between these modes? We need to justify Private to procurement.
[06:05] Lena: Private has higher fixed costs (deployment, ops) but predictable unit cost—Dedicated sits in the middle with reserved capacity pricing; Hosted is variable usage. We'll send a sample TCO sheet comparing per-token cost, reserved capacity, and ops overhead.
[06:19] Trevor: Another ask — we need to prove SOC2/ISO and run regular pen tests. Do you provide penetration test evidence and third-party audit reports?
[06:29] Priya: Yes — we can share SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts for our control plane. For Private we can provide deployment checklists and assist in customer pen test scoping. Where Redwood controls the compute we can coordinate and provide necessary attestations.
[06:44] Noah (Legal): We need contractual clauses for data processing addendum — data controller vs processor language and breach notification SLAs.
[06:52] Lena: We'll share our standard DPA and can accommodate specific contractual language for enterprise deals.
[06:58] [07:00] Sarah: There was also mention of tokenization and KV cache — if we enable caching to improve latency, how do we ensure cached keys don't leak PII across tenants?
[07:10] Miguel: Caching is namespaced by tenant and by key. KV cache entries are encrypted at rest with tenant-specific keys. For maximum safety, you can disable persistent cache and use ephemeral session cache only.
[07:22] Aisha: Do you support per-tenant encryption keys so even if underlying disks are shared, the data is discoverable only with tenant keys?
[07:29] Priya: Yes, envelope encryption with tenant-specific keys is supported. In Private, tenants can bring KMS keys; in Dedicated we can do tenant keys in the Redwood-managed KMS with strict access controls.
[07:41] [07:41] Trevor: For HIPAA-bound data, do you recommend Private only, or is Dedicated acceptable with certain compensating controls?
[07:48] Miguel: It depends. Dedicated can be configured to meet HIPAA if you control the keys and ensure your VPC/network segmentation meets the requirements. Often larger customers prefer Private for the extra assurance, but Dedicated is used by customers who want isolation without full ops ownership.
[08:02] Lena: Quick check — what's your timeline for pilot and compliance sign-off?
[08:07] Sarah: We'd like to run a pilot in Q2 and aim for production later in Q3, but that hinges on legal/infosec sign-off in the next 4–6 weeks.
[08:16] Miguel: We can move quickly on the hosted benchmark in days; Private deployment may need a couple of weeks to provision and validate. We'll scope a minimal pilot that demonstrates residency and auditing.
[08:28] Noah: On evidence collection — we may have auditors asking for a demo where we show logs, key rotation records, and operator access audit trails. Can you simulate that?
[08:37] Priya: Yes — we can prepare an audit package and demo playbook. For hosted we'll show redacted flows; for Private we'll show full artifacts inside your environment.
[08:48] [08:48] Evan: Procurement question — if we sign for Dedicated reserved capacity, is there a break clause if regulators demand Private-only?
[08:57] Lena: We can negotiate transition terms into contract — it's a commercial conversation, but we typically include migration support and credits for migration in enterprise agreements.
[09:06] Sarah: Are there any limitations around model variants and quantization in Private? We rely on quantized weights for lower cost.
[09:14] Miguel: We support quantized model variants across all deployment modes. The runtime is the same; kernel selection and quantization-friendly execution paths are available in Private and Dedicated. Host policies may differ if you're using Redwood-hosted curated models.
[09:31] [09:31] Trevor: One more technical: how do you handle data residency when backend dependencies (metrics, tracing) are in a central control plane?
[09:40] Priya: For Private, metrics/tracing can be streamed to your observability stack inside region. For Dedicated we can mirror metrics to your tenant bucket. If you need zero cross-region telemetry, we run the control plane connectors inside your VPC.
[09:54] Miguel: Also, we support per-route telemetry redaction and sampling so sensitive request payloads are never persisted outside your tenancy.
[10:05] Lena: OK let's recap and capture actions.
[10:09] Lena: Action items — we'll share SOC2 artifacts, Private deployment diagram, KMS deep dive scheduling options, and a benchmark plan. Miguel will own the benchmark template. Trevor/Noah will share the regulatory matrix.
[10:21] Sarah: Sounds good. Can you also include a short checklist for what Redwood needs from us to spin up a Private pilot?
[10:28] Priya: Yes — we'll provide a one-page readiness checklist (VPC subnets, peering, KMS endpoints, firewall rules, IP allowlist, contact list).
[10:36] Evan: Timelines — if you send the diagram and checklist this week, we can align legal and infra in the next 10 business days.
[10:44] Lena: We'll follow up with calendar invites for the KMS deep dive and the benchmarking kickoff.
[10:50] Miguel: One note — competitors often push the hosted convenience line but fall short on operator access controls. We'll include specifics about how operator access is audited and how to disable remote ops entirely if desired.
[11:04] Trevor: Appreciate that. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood retains telemetry for debugging and for how long? We need retention windows documented.
[11:11] Priya: We'll document default retention, and show how to adjust per stream; in Private you control retention store so you meet your 7-year requirement if needed.
[11:22] Lena: Great. Final Q: any blockers from your side to start a hosted benchmark?
[11:28] Sarah: No blockers. We'll share a small prompt/test set, and the legal matrix and we'll be ready.
[11:35] Lena: Thanks everyone — we'll get those artifacts over.

End of transcript.
